name: exit
purpose: MS C 5.x exit(). Runs the (empty) atexit/XI near-function table (037d) three times and the far-function table (038c) once, then calls _nullcheck (07a2); if the DGROUP null-area checksum failed and status==0, status is changed to 255. Closes DOS handles 5..19 whose _osfile flag byte at 0x528e+h has bit0 set (INT 21h AH=3Eh), calls 0350 to restore interrupt vectors, then terminates with INT 21h AH=4Ch AL=status. Never returns.

0x528e.name: g_crt_osfile
0x528e.meaning: MS C _osfile handle flag array (bit0 = handle open)

notes: Ghidra's decompile hides the AH values; from asm: AH=3Eh close, AH=4Ch terminate. Called by TOWN/MAINOUT/DUNGEON to quit the game.

name: crt_restore_vectors
purpose: Exit-time cleanup used by exit(): if the far hook at 0x6ace/0x6ad0 is non-null it is called far with BX=2 (floating-point/8087 termination hook, unused in this game); restores INT 00h (divide error) to the vector saved at 0x5273 with INT 21h AH=25h; if the byte flag at 0x52b0 is set, also restores the interrupt whose number is in 0x52b1 to the vector saved at 0x52b2 (AH=25h).

0x6ace.name: g_crt_fp_term_hook
0x6ace.meaning: far function pointer called at exit if segment word 0x6ad0 != 0 (CRT fp termination hook); zero in DATA.OVL

0x5273.name: g_crt_saved_int0_vec
0x5273.meaning: original INT 00h vector saved by CRT startup

0x52b0.name: g_crt_saved_int_flag
0x52b0.meaning: nonzero if a second interrupt vector was hooked by startup

0x52b1.name: g_crt_saved_int_num
0x52b1.meaning: interrupt number of the second saved vector

0x52b2.name: g_crt_saved_int_vec
0x52b2.meaning: original vector of the second hooked interrupt

notes: INT 21h AH=25h (set vector). Not needed in a port.

name: crt_run_near_fn_table
purpose: Walks a table of near function pointers backwards from DI down to SI and calls each non-null entry (atexit / C initialiser-terminator table runner). In this executable every call passes SI==DI (empty tables at 0xa9bc and 0x6ada), so it is a no-op.
notes: Register-parameter assembly routine.

name: crt_run_far_fn_table
purpose: Same as 037d but the table holds 4-byte far pointers; each non-null entry is called with CALLF. Called with an empty range (0x6ada..0x6ada), so a no-op here.
notes: Register-parameter assembly routine.

name: __aFuldiv
proto: unsigned long __aFuldiv(unsigned long dividend, unsigned long divisor)
purpose: MS C unsigned 32-bit division helper. Args on stack (dividend low,high then divisor low,high), result in DX:AX. Fast path when the divisor's high word is 0 (two 16-bit DIVs); otherwise shifts both operands right until the divisor fits in 16 bits, divides, multiplies back and corrects the quotient down by one if the product overshoots. Callee cleans 8 bytes of stack.
notes: Remainder is not returned.

name: memchr
proto: char *memchr(const char *buf, int ch, unsigned n)
purpose: Scans n bytes of buf for the byte ch (REPNE SCASB). Returns pointer to the first match, or NULL if n==0 or not found.

name: itoa
purpose: MS C itoa(): loads value into AX, sign-extends into DX only when radix==10 (so negative decimal numbers get a '-'), sets BL=1 (signed flag), DI=buf, CX=radix and tail-jumps into the shared conversion routine 07d6, which returns buf.

name: __aFlmul
purpose: MS C 32-bit multiply helper: returns a*b in DX:AX (low 32 bits). Fast path when both high words are zero; otherwise lo*lo + (hi_a*lo_b + lo_a*hi_b)<<16. Callee cleans 8 bytes.

name: long_shl_inplace
purpose: Loads the 32-bit value at *value into DX:AX, shifts it left by count (via 082a) and stores it back. Compiler helper for '*p <<= n' on longs. Callee cleans 4 bytes.
notes: Used by TALK overlay.

name: __aFldiv
purpose: MS C signed 32-bit division helper. Negates negative operands, counting sign changes, performs the same unsigned algorithm as 03a0, then negates the quotient if exactly one operand was negative. Result DX:AX; callee cleans 8 bytes.

name: crt_find_rterr_msg
purpose: Looks up a run-time error message in the CRT table at DGROUP 0xa452: a sequence of {int id; char text[]} records terminated by id -1. Returns pointer to the text for id==msgno, or NULL if the terminator is reached. Messages: 0 'R6000 stack overflow', 3 'R6003 integer divide by 0', 9 'R6009 not enough space for environment', 0xfc '\r\n', 0xff 'run-time error ', 1 'R6001 null pointer assignment', 2 'R6002 floating point not loaded'.

0xa452.name: g_crt_rterr_msgs
0xa452.meaning: MS C run-time error message table, terminated by id -1

notes: Ghidra shows the table start as s____CONFLICT_____1f64_a448+10.

name: crt_write_rterr_msg
purpose: Finds the message for msgno via 0532 and, if found, writes it (strlen bytes) to DOS handle 2 (stderr) with INT 21h AH=40h.
notes: INT 21h AH=40h BX=2.

name: crt_rterr_prefix
purpose: Prints the run-time error banner: message 0xfc ('\r\n'), then calls the optional near hook at 0x52b6 if non-null, then message 0xff ('run-time error '). The caller then prints the specific Rxxxx message.

0x52b6.name: g_crt_rterr_hook
0x52b6.meaning: optional CRT hook called before 'run-time error ' text (zero)

name: _nullcheck
purpose: MS C null-pointer-assignment check run at exit: XORs together the first 0x42 bytes of DGROUP (the 'MS Run-Time Library - Copyright...' area) and expects 0x55. If the checksum differs, prints 'run-time error R6001 - null pointer assignment' to stderr (0586 + 055d(1)) and returns 1; otherwise returns a value whose high byte is 0 (treated as success by exit()).

0x0000.name: g_crt_null_area
0x0000.meaning: DGROUP null-pointer guard area (copyright string); checksum must stay 0x55

notes: The on-disk DATA.OVL has a 16-byte header: DGROUP offset X = DATA.OVL file offset X+0x10 (verified: checksum of file bytes 0x10..0x51 is 0x55, and the wiki's 0x541E scancode table is at DGROUP 0x540e).

name: crt_xtoa_core
purpose: Shared body of itoa/ltoa/ultoa. If BL!=0, radix==10 and the value is negative, emits '-' and negates DX:AX. Repeatedly divides the 32-bit value by the radix, emitting digits '0'-'9' then 'a'-'z' (adds 0x27 for >9) in reverse order, writes a NUL, then reverses the digit run in place. Returns the original buffer pointer in AX and also pops the caller's frame (shared epilogue with 0426).
notes: Register-parameter assembly; entered by JMP from 0426.

name: __aFlshl
purpose: Shifts the 32-bit value DX:AX left by CL bits (CH cleared first); no-op when count is 0.
notes: Register-parameter assembly helper.

name: restore_video_mode
purpose: If a BIOS video mode was saved in g_saved_video_mode (0x5304 != -1), restores it with INT 10h AH=00h AL=mode. Called by the overlays before exit().

0x5304.name: g_saved_video_mode
0x5304.meaning: BIOS video mode saved before the driver switched modes; -1 = none (DATA.OVL initial value 0xffff)

notes: INT 10h AH=0.

name: init_graphics_driver
purpose: If a driver is loaded (g_drv_seg != 0): when set_mode!=0 and no mode saved yet, saves the current BIOS mode (INT 10h AH=0Fh, AL) into g_saved_video_mode; then calls driver entry 1 (offset 3) with AX=set_mode and BX=0x52ba (pointer to the graphics config block in DGROUP). The driver stores BX and, if AX!=0, switches video mode via INT 10h.

0x5350.name: g_drv_entry_off
0x5350.meaning: driver jump-table offset (entry*3); far pointer low word used for CALLF

0x5352.name: g_drv_seg
0x5352.meaning: segment of loaded graphics driver (0 = none)

0x52ba.name: g_gfx_config
0x52ba.meaning: graphics config block passed to the driver (52ba: force-CGA flag/word; 52bc,52be: cell width,height=8,8; 52c0,52c2: tile width,height=16,16; 52c4 clip enable; 52c8 adapter type; ...; driver stores its draw-page word at +0x1e = 0x52d8)

notes: No callers in catalog (INTRO calls the +0x10 artifact 08a2, so INTRO is the real caller). Driver is register-called: AX, BX.

name: clip_test_point
purpose: Register helper: returns carry clear if (x,y) lies inside the clip window [g_clip_xmin..g_clip_xmax] x [g_clip_ymin..g_clip_ymax], carry set otherwise.
notes: Result is in CF only; Ghidra shows an empty if.

name: normalize_rect
purpose: Register helper: swaps endpoints so that AX<=CX and BX<=DX, then clamps every coordinate to the screen (x to 0..319, y to 0..199).

name: clip_line
proto: bool clip_line(/*AX=x1,BX=y1,CX=x2,DX=y2*/) -> CF (1=rejected), clipped coords in AX..DX
purpose: Cohen-Sutherland style line clipper against the clip window. Computes outcodes for both endpoints (0a22); if both are zero returns CF=0 unchanged; if the outcodes share a bit the line is entirely outside and CF=1 is returned. Otherwise each outside endpoint is moved onto the window edge by the bisection routine 0991 (saving intermediate results in 0x52fa..0x5300), and the clipped endpoints are returned in AX,BX,CX,DX with CF=0.
notes: Register-parameter assembly; decompiled C is unreliable here.

name: clip_bisect_endpoint
proto: void clip_bisect_endpoint(/*AX,BX=outside point; CX,DX=other point*/) -> AX,BX on window edge
purpose: Moves the outside endpoint (AX,BX) toward (CX,DX) by repeated midpoint bisection (signed halving) until it lands exactly on a clip edge (x==xmin/xmax or y==ymin/ymax) or the remaining step (max of |dx|,|dy| in 0x52f6/0x52f8) is below 1. Recomputes outcodes each step via 0a22; while still outside it keeps halving.
notes: Register-parameter assembly.

name: clip_outcodes
purpose: Computes 4-bit outcodes against the clip window for two points: bit0 x<xmin, bit1 x>xmax, bit2 y>ymax, bit3 y<ymin. Returns them in SI and DI.
notes: Ghidra decompiled it as an empty function.

name: set_color
purpose: Sets the current drawing colour. If color != -1 it is masked to 0..15 (or 0..3 when the adapter type g_adapter_type==0, CGA) and stored in g_cur_color; then driver entry 15 (offset 0x2d) is called with AL=colour. If color == -1, g_cur_color is set to -1 (which disables plot_pixel / clear_window colour) and the driver is not called.

0x5350.name: g_drv_entry_off
0x5350.meaning: driver jump-table offset (entry*3); far pointer low word used for CALLF

0x5352.name: g_drv_seg
0x5352.meaning: segment of loaded graphics driver (0 = none)

notes: Driver takes colour in AL.

name: fill_rect
proto: void fill_rect(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)  /* pascal: AX,BX,CX,DX */
purpose: Normalises/clamps the rectangle (08e6) and calls driver entry 21 (offset 0x3f) with CF=0 to fill it with the current colour. Pascal convention: args pushed left to right, callee cleans 8 bytes; Ghidra call sites therefore show the arguments reversed (e.g. FUN_0aa6(199,0x13f,0,0) is fill_rect(0,0,319,199)).

0x5350.name: g_drv_entry_off
0x5350.meaning: driver jump-table offset (entry*3); far pointer low word used for CALLF

0x5352.name: g_drv_seg
0x5352.meaning: segment of loaded graphics driver (0 = none)

notes: CF=1 variant is 0b86 (XOR fill).

name: copy_rect_between_pages
proto: int copy_rect_between_pages(int src_page, int dst_page, int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)  /* pascal: SI,DI,AX,BX,CX,DX */
purpose: Copies a screen rectangle between the two video pages. Requires src_page != dst_page and both in {0,1}; otherwise does nothing. Normalises the rect (08e6), sets CF = (src_page != 0) and calls driver entry 8 (offset 0x18), which copies page0->page1 when CF=0 and page1->page0 when CF=1. Returns whatever the driver leaves in AX.

0x5350.name: g_drv_entry_off
0x5350.meaning: driver jump-table offset (entry*3); far pointer low word used for CALLF

0x5352.name: g_drv_seg
0x5352.meaning: segment of loaded graphics driver (0 = none)

notes: Ghidra shows args reversed (DUNGEON: FUN_0ace(0xb2,y,0xe,y2,0,1) = copy page0->page1 of rect (14,y)-(178,y2)). Which of SI/DI is source is inferred from the EGA driver (CF=0 path = drv entry 9's AX=0,BX=1 path).

name: draw_line
proto: void draw_line(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)  /* pascal */
purpose: Draws a line in the current colour: loads AX..DX from the (left-to-right) args, clears CF (normal, non-XOR drawing) and calls the line core 0b2d. Updates the pen position to (x2,y2).
notes: Ghidra call-site args appear reversed.

name: line_core
purpose: Shared line renderer. Stores (x2,y2) into g_pen_x/g_pen_y, saves the flags (XOR flag in CF), and if g_clip_enabled runs clip_line (0935), returning early if the line is rejected. Then dispatches on the (clipped) endpoints: y1==y2 && x1==x2 -> driver 16 (pixel); y1==y2 -> normalise + driver 19 (horizontal line); x1==x2 -> normalise + driver 20 (vertical line); else driver 17 (general line). The saved CF is restored (POPF) before the driver call so the driver sees the XOR flag.

0x52c4.name: g_clip_enabled
0x52c4.meaning: nonzero = software clipping to g_clip_* window is enabled

0x5350.name: g_drv_entry_off
0x5350.meaning: driver jump-table offset (entry*3); far pointer low word used for CALLF

0x5352.name: g_drv_seg
0x5352.meaning: segment of loaded graphics driver (0 = none)

notes: Register-parameter assembly; decompiled C is garbage (flag-register arithmetic).

name: fill_rect_xor
proto: void fill_rect_xor(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)  /* pascal */
purpose: Same as fill_rect but calls driver entry 21 with CF=1, which makes the EGA driver select the XOR raster op (GC function register = 0x18) so the rectangle is inverted/XORed with the current colour (used for highlight boxes).

0x5350.name: g_drv_entry_off
0x5350.meaning: driver jump-table offset (entry*3); far pointer low word used for CALLF

0x5352.name: g_drv_seg
0x5352.meaning: segment of loaded graphics driver (0 = none)

notes: Ghidra call-site args reversed.

name: load_image_file
proto: int load_image_file(char *name)  /* pascal; returns segment or 0/-1 */
purpose: Loads a graphics file (e.g. TILES.16, DNGx.16, END1.16) with load_file (125d, which LZW-decompresses unless the name is in the raw-file list). On success AX=size, BX=segment and driver entry 22 (offset 0x42) is called, which walks the file's header (count + per-image {width,height,offset} entries) and converts each image's bit layout into the driver's planar format in place; the segment (BX) is returned. On failure: BX==0 -> returns -1 (cannot actually occur: that case exits), else stores the DOS error code in g_last_dos_error and calls the far error hook g_error_hook (which displays a disk error), returns 0.

0x535c.name: g_last_dos_error
0x535c.meaning: last DOS error code / disk-error flag (1 set by INT 24h handler)

0x5394.name: g_error_hook
0x5394.meaning: far pointer to the disk-error handler in ROOT (1000:2320/2322/25ca), called with g_last_dos_error set

0x5350.name: g_drv_entry_off
0x5350.meaning: driver jump-table offset (entry*3); far pointer low word used for CALLF

0x5352.name: g_drv_seg
0x5352.meaning: segment of loaded graphics driver (0 = none)

notes: Driver entry 22 semantics from EGA.DRV drv_22_1226/FUN_123f/FUN_17be (bit-plane shuffle).

name: free_far_block
purpose: Frees the DOS memory block whose segment is seg: ES=seg, INT 21h AH=49h. Used to release buffers obtained from load_file / dos_alloc.
notes: Identical copy at 0fdc.

name: draw_image_alt
proto: void draw_image_alt(unsigned seg, int index, int x, int y, int mode)  /* pascal: AX,BX,SI,DI,CX */
purpose: Same register setup as draw_image (0d4c) but calls driver entry 33 (offset 0x63). In EGA.DRV entry 33 is an alias of entry 25 (drv_25_12b4, the image blitter); other drivers may implement a variant. Draws image number index from the image file loaded at segment seg at pixel (x,y); CX=mode is passed through (callers use 0 or a flag value).

0x5350.name: g_drv_entry_off
0x5350.meaning: driver jump-table offset (entry*3); far pointer low word used for CALLF

0x5352.name: g_drv_seg
0x5352.meaning: segment of loaded graphics driver (0 = none)

notes: Only DUNGEON uses it. Ghidra call sites show args reversed: FUN_0bfc(mode,y,x,index,seg).

name: set_draw_page
purpose: Selects the video page (0 or 1) that subsequent drawing targets: driver entry 5 (offset 0xf) with AX=page; the driver stores it at config+0x1e (DGROUP 0x52d8) when valid.

0x5350.name: g_drv_entry_off
0x5350.meaning: driver jump-table offset (entry*3); far pointer low word used for CALLF

0x5352.name: g_drv_seg
0x5352.meaning: segment of loaded graphics driver (0 = none)

0x52d8.name: g_draw_page
0x52d8.meaning: current drawing page as stored by the driver (config block +0x1e)

name: set_clip_window
proto: void set_clip_window(int xmin, int ymin, int xmax, int ymax)  /* pascal */
purpose: Stores the software clipping rectangle: g_clip_xmin=AX, g_clip_ymin=BX, g_clip_xmax=CX, g_clip_ymax=DX. Clipping is only applied when g_clip_enabled (0x52c4) is nonzero (set by DUNGEON code).
notes: Only DUNGEON calls it; Ghidra shows args reversed.

name: plot_pixel
proto: void plot_pixel(int x, int y)  /* pascal: AX,BX */
purpose: Sets the pen position to (x,y). If g_cur_color != -1: when clipping is enabled and the point is outside the clip window (08ca) nothing is drawn; otherwise driver entry 16 (offset 0x30) plots the pixel at (AX,BX) in the current colour with CF=0.
notes: Ghidra call-site args reversed.

name: draw_hline
proto: void draw_hline(int x1, int y, int x2)  /* pascal: AX,BX,CX */
purpose: Horizontal line from (x1,y) to (x2,y) in the current colour. Sets g_pen_x=x2; if clipping is enabled, rejects the line unless both x's lie inside [g_clip_xmin..g_clip_xmax] and 0..319 (0ccd; y is not checked); then driver entry 19 (offset 0x39) with AX=x1, BX=y, CX=x2, CF=0.
notes: Ghidra call sites show (x2,y,x1), e.g. FUN_0c9c(0x107,0x50,0xf0) = draw_hline(240,80,263).

name: clip_test_hline
purpose: Register helper for draw_hline: orders x1>=x2 in AX/CX and returns CF=0 only if max(x) >= g_clip_xmin, min(x) <= g_clip_xmax and both in 0..319; CF=1 otherwise.
notes: Note the comparison is loose (min against xmax, max against xmin); matches the original.

name: draw_vline
proto: void draw_vline(int x, int y1, int y2)  /* pascal: AX,BX,DX */
purpose: Vertical line at x from y1 to y2. Sets g_pen_y=y2, orders y1<=y2, if clipping enabled rejects unless y1 >= g_clip_ymin, y2 <= g_clip_ymax and both in 0..199 (0d2b); then driver entry 20 (offset 0x3c) with AX=CX=x, BX=y1, DX=y2, CF=0.
notes: Ghidra call-site args reversed.

name: clip_test_vline
purpose: Register helper for draw_vline: CF=0 if y1 >= g_clip_ymin, y2 <= g_clip_ymax, y1 >= 0 and both y's <= 199; CF=1 otherwise.

name: draw_image
proto: void draw_image(unsigned seg, int index, int x, int y, int mode)  /* pascal: AX,BX,SI,DI,CX */
purpose: Blits image number index from the converted image file at segment seg (loaded by load_image_file / load_picture_file) to pixel position (x,y) via driver entry 25 (offset 0x4b, the driver's bitmap blitter). CX=mode is passed through (0 in nearly all calls; DUNGEON passes a flag). Used for title/end-game pictures, dungeon walls, character-creation art.
notes: Ghidra call sites show args reversed: FUN_0d4c(mode,y,x,index,seg) e.g. FUN_0d4c(0,0,0xd8,0,seg) = draw_image(seg,0,216,0,0). Exact meaning of mode not determined (driver-internal).

name: draw_stacked_pictures
purpose: Switches drawing to page 1, sets colour 0 and fills the whole screen (fill_rect(0,0,319,199)), then for i=0..6 draws picture i of the file at pic_seg horizontally centred (x = (320 - g_pic_widths[i]) / 2) at y = running sum of g_pic_heights[0..i-1] via draw_image_masked (1044). Finally switches back to page 0 and calls driver_set_speed (1140). The width table is 24,40,72,112,152,216,280 and heights 3,7,11,20,32,45,61 - a growing stack of strips (the intro/title artwork).

0x5306.name: g_pic_widths
0x5306.meaning: pixel widths of the 7 stacked title pictures (24,40,72,112,152,216,280)

0x5314.name: g_pic_heights
0x5314.meaning: pixel heights of the 7 stacked pictures (3,7,11,20,32,45,61)

notes: Real caller is INTRO via the +0x10 artifact 0d82. Which picture file is used is decided by the caller.

name: detect_video_adapter
purpose: Hardware autodetect (no callers found - probably dead/unused). Reads the BIOS machine id byte at F000:FFFE: 0xFD (PCjr) or 0xFF (PC) -> g_machine_class=0, 0xFC (AT) -> 2, else 6. For id 0xFF it scans F000:A000.. for the string 'Tandy' (g_str_tandy at 0x5322); if found sets g_machine_class=3 and adapter type 2 (Tandy 1000). For non-PCjr machines it then calls INT 10h AH=12h BL=10h (EGA info): if CX!=-1 an EGA is present -> type 1 for colour (BH=0) or -1 (unsupported mono EGA). Otherwise INT 10h AH=0Fh: mode 7 -> polls port 3BAh bit 7 up to 32768 times; if it toggles -> type 3 (Hercules); else type 0 (CGA). PCjr -> CGA. Result stored in g_adapter_type.

0x5322.name: g_str_tandy
0x5322.meaning: "Tandy" signature string searched in the BIOS ROM

notes: Zero callers in catalog. The port can skip this: the EGA path (type 1) is what the Rust port emulates.

name: load_video_driver
purpose: Ghidra function boundary is wrong: the real function starts at 1000:0e94 (16 bytes earlier; the +0x10 INTRO call-target offset hides it). load_video_driver(): if g_adapter_type == -1 returns immediately. Otherwise picks the adapter from command-line/config flags: g_force_cga (0x52ba)!=0 -> 0 (CGA); else g_flag_ega (0x52ef)!=0 -> 1; else g_flag_herc (0x52f3)!=0 -> 3; else g_flag_tandy (0x52f1)!=0 -> 2; (else leaves g_adapter_type as is). For Tandy (type 2) it allocates 0x400 paragraphs (16 KB) with dos_alloc (15c6) - exiting via INT 21h AH=4Ch on failure - and stores the segment at 0050:0010 (Tandy video RAM relocation word), then uses index 2. Loads the driver file named by g_drv_names[type] (CGA.DRV / EGA.DRV / T1K.DRV / HER.DRV) with load_file (125d) and stores the returned segment in g_drv_seg; the loaded file starts with the 38-entry jump table. On load failure: BX==0 -> returns -1, else sets g_last_dos_error=AX, calls g_error_hook and returns 0.

0x52ba.name: g_force_cga
0x52ba.meaning: nonzero = use CGA driver (set by INTRO from options)

notes: Record originally written under artifact address 0ea4; real function starts at 0e94.

name: driver_init_screen
purpose: Ghidra boundary is wrong; the real function starts at 1000:0f2a. driver_init_screen(): calls driver entry 2 (offset 6) with CF=1 and stores the returned AX into g_scratch_seg (0x5354). In EGA.DRV entry 2 sets up the second video page (0xA800), clears 32 KB of video memory, programs the EGA graphics controller, and returns a segment that the loader then uses as the 12 KB LZW dictionary/scratch area (see 135a).

0x5354.name: g_scratch_seg
0x5354.meaning: scratch segment returned by driver entry 2; used as LZW dictionary (0x1800 words) during file loads

notes: Record originally written under artifact address 0f3a; real function starts at 0f2a.

name: rect_effect
proto: int rect_effect(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)  /* pascal */
purpose: Normalises the rectangle and calls driver entry 34 (offset 0x66) with CF=0. In EGA.DRV the CF=0 path of entry 34 visits every pixel of the rectangle in pseudo-random (LFSR) order calling an internal per-pixel routine - a 'dissolve' style screen wipe/fill of the rect. Used by ENDGAME (whole screen), BLCKTHRN and SJOG.
notes: Ghidra call site ENDGAME: FUN_0f46(199,0x13f,0,0) = rect_effect(0,0,319,199).

name: copy_page
proto: void copy_page(int src_page, int dst_page)  /* pascal: AX,BX */
purpose: If src_page != dst_page calls driver entry 9 (offset 0x1b) with AX=src, BX=dst, which copies the whole video page 0->1 or 1->0 (page flip by copy). Used after drawing a full frame on the hidden page.

name: draw_line_to
proto: void draw_line_to(int x2, int y2)  /* pascal: CX,DX */
purpose: Draws a line from the current pen position (g_pen_x,g_pen_y) to (x2,y2) with CF=0 via line_core (0b2d), leaving the pen at (x2,y2).

name: load_file_to_mem
proto: unsigned load_file_to_mem(char *name)  /* pascal; returns segment, 0 on error */
purpose: Loads a data file via load_file (125d): allocates a DOS block and reads/decompresses the file into it. On success returns the segment (BX). On failure: if BX==0 returns -1 (unreachable: load_file exits on out-of-memory), else records the DOS error code in g_last_dos_error, calls the far g_error_hook and returns 0.
notes: Callers free the block later with free_far_block.

name: free_far_block2
purpose: Byte-for-byte duplicate of free_far_block (0be4): INT 21h AH=49h with ES=seg to free a DOS memory block.
notes: Duplicate of 0be4.

name: load_picture_file
purpose: Loads a picture file (e.g. PROPORT.PCS, CREATE.16) with load_file, then calls driver entry 24 (offset 0x48) with AX=size, BX=segment, CX=size-1; the EGA driver stores BX as its 'current picture segment' and converts the picture's bit layout to planar form. Returns 1 on success. On failure returns -1 if BX==0 (unreachable) else sets g_last_dos_error, calls g_error_hook, returns 0. The picture is released later by free_picture (102e).
notes: Pairs with 1044 (draw_image_masked) and 102e.

name: free_picture
purpose: Calls driver entry 30 (offset 0x5a); in EGA.DRV this frees (INT 21h) the picture segment registered by entry 24 if one is set.

name: draw_image_masked
proto: void draw_image_masked(unsigned seg, int index, int x, int y)  /* pascal: AX,BX,SI,DI */
purpose: Draws image index from the picture file at segment seg (registered via load_picture_file) at pixel (x,y) using driver entry 26 (offset 0x4e). The EGA driver reads the image table in the segment (count at 0, pointers at 2+2*i, image = {width,height,bits}) and ORs the bits into all four planes after clearing them (AND/OR), i.e. a masked/transparent blit at arbitrary x. Used by FONT for proportional-font glyphs (index = char-0x20) and by draw_stacked_pictures.
notes: Ghidra call sites reversed: FUN_1044(y,x,index,seg).

name: tile_transition_effect
proto: int tile_transition_effect(int tile, int col, int row)  /* pascal: SI,AX,BX */
purpose: Runs a 256-step animated effect at map cell (col,row) with tile number tile: for step=0..255 (step in DI) it calls driver entry 34 (offset 0x66) with CF=1, AX=col, BX=row, SI=tile, CX/DX=g_cell_w/g_cell_h, DI=step. Every 8 steps it polls for a keypress: if g_input_mode (0x5893)=='B' via vec_FONT_e4dc(1), otherwise via FUN_1000_5910(); a nonzero result from the FONT routine aborts the effect and is returned. Returns 0 when all 256 steps complete. In EGA.DRV the CF=1 path draws progressively more pixels of the tile in LFSR order - a dissolve/materialise of one tile (used e.g. when 'Thou dost see' an object appear).

0x5893.name: g_input_mode
0x5893.meaning: input/command mode byte; 'B' selects the FONT-overlay key poll

notes: Two driver calls per loop iteration with DI incremented between them. Ghidra call sites reversed: FUN_1068(row,col,tile).

name: draw_tile
proto: void draw_tile(int tile, int col, int row)  /* pascal: BX, AL, AH */
purpose: Draws a 16x16 map tile: AX = (row<<8)|col, BX = tile number, CX/DX = g_cell_w/g_cell_h (8,8: pixel origin of the map view), SI/DI = g_tile_w/g_tile_h (16,16); driver entry 27 (offset 0x51). The EGA driver copies the 128-byte (4 planes x 32 bytes) tile bitmap from its tile segment to video memory at x = 8 + col*16, y = 8 + row*16 using the plane-write mask, with a fast path for 16x16.
notes: Ghidra call sites reversed: FUN_10e0(row,col,tile).

name: draw_effect_frame
proto: void draw_effect_frame(int frame, int col, int row)  /* pascal: AX,SI,DI */
purpose: Calls driver entry 32 (offset 0x60) with CF=1, AX=frame, SI=col, DI=row, BL=g_input_mode byte (0x5893) and CX/DX=g_cell_w/g_cell_h. Callers run it with frame counting down 15..1 with a short delay between calls at a map cell (ROOT 48a8/56ac, FONT), so entry 32 (a 1.3 KB driver routine) renders one frame of a per-tile animation (e.g. a spell/flash effect). Exact visual not determined.

0x5893.name: g_input_mode
0x5893.meaning: mode byte passed to the driver in BL

notes: Ghidra call sites reversed: FUN_1112(row,col,frame).

name: driver_set_speed
purpose: Passes the CPU speed factor g_cpu_speed (0x5356, measured by calibrate_timer) to driver entry 37 (offset 0x6f) in AX so the driver can scale its delay loops (sound/animation timing).

0x5356.name: g_cpu_speed
0x5356.meaning: CPU speed factor = loop iterations per 55 ms tick * 18 / 750

name: init_system
purpose: Startup for the engine layer: installs the INT 24h critical-error handler (code at 1000:1233: sets g_last_dos_error=1 and returns AL=0 'ignore') and an INT 23h Ctrl-Break handler (1000:1247: just IRET, so Ctrl-C is ignored) with INT 21h AH=25h; then init_text_windows (1184), reset_text_attrs (1226) and calibrate_timer (11b4).

0x535c.name: g_last_dos_error
0x535c.meaning: last DOS error code; set to 1 by the INT 24h critical-error handler

0x5394.name: g_error_hook
0x5394.meaning: far pointer to ROOT disk-error handler (1000:2320/2322/25ca)

notes: Real caller is INTRO (via artifact 1168). The INT 1Ch hook is installed only temporarily by 11b4.

name: init_text_windows
purpose: Initialises the four 8-byte text window records at 0x535e to x0=0,y0=0,x1=39,y1=24,curx=0,cury=0,attr=0x0f,flags=0, sets g_cur_window_ptr to window 0 and g_cur_window=0.

0x535e.name: g_text_windows
0x535e.meaning: 4 text windows in 8x8 cells: x0,y0,x1,y1 inclusive bounds (default 0,0,39,24), curx/cury cursor relative to x0/y0, attr = bg<<4|fg (default 0x0f), flags bit0 underline, bit1 centred, bit2 inverse

0x539a.name: g_cur_window_ptr
0x539a.meaning: near pointer to current window record in g_text_windows

name: calibrate_timer
purpose: Measures CPU speed: hooks INT 1Ch (timer tick, 18.2 Hz) with the handler at 1000:1214 (which just increments g_tick_counter 0x535a), waits for a tick, then counts how many times it can increment g_cpu_speed (0x5356) before the next tick, restores the old INT 1Ch vector (INT 21h AH=35h/25h), and scales the count: g_cpu_speed = count*18/750. Finally stores the conventional memory size in KB from INT 12h into g_mem_kb (0x5358). g_cpu_speed is later passed to the driver (1140) and used to scale delays (e.g. 20fa, 1dda).

0x5356.name: g_cpu_speed
0x5356.meaning: CPU speed factor (loop iterations per tick *18/750)

0x535a.name: g_tick_counter
0x535a.meaning: incremented by the temporary INT 1Ch handler

notes: Interrupt handler bodies at 1214 (INT 1Ch), 1233 (INT 24h), 1247 (INT 23h) were disassembled from raw bytes. A port can set g_cpu_speed to a constant.

name: reset_text_attrs

0x53a4.name: g_text_underline
0x53a4.meaning: 1 = underline glyphs (last glyph row forced to 0xff)

0x53a6.name: g_text_centred
0x53a6.meaning: 1 = print_string centres each line (window flag bit1)

name: fatal_out_of_memory
purpose: Fatal exit used by load_file when a DOS allocation fails: INT 10h AX=0003 (80x25 text mode), INT 21h AH=09h prints g_str_out_of_memory ('Out of Memory...\r\n$' at 0x53e6), INT 21h AX=4C01h terminates with code 1, followed by a self-jump.

0x53e6.name: g_str_out_of_memory
0x53e6.meaning: "Out of Memory...\r\n$" ($-terminated DOS string). Its tail (0x53ea..) doubles as the glyph backup buffer, so it is clobbered once text has been printed.

notes: Entered by JMP from 125d/135a error paths; never returns.

name: load_file
proto: /* DX=name */ load_file() -> CF=0: AX=size (low word, or -1 if 0), BX=segment; CF=1: BX=1 file error (AX=DOS code) or BX=0
purpose: Core file loader (register convention). If the name is in the raw-file list (1588 finds it in g_raw_file_names at 0x25ea: PROPORT.PCS, BRITISH.BIT, TITLE.BIT, TILES.16, ITEMS.16, DNG1.16...), the file is loaded uncompressed: size via get_file_size (1654), block of (size-1)/16+1 paragraphs via dos_alloc (15c6; failure -> fatal_out_of_memory), contents read with read_file_into_seg (160e; on failure the block is freed and CF=1,BX=1). Otherwise it is an LZW file: opens it (INT 21h AH=3Dh AL=2), reads the 4-byte uncompressed size into g_lzw_orig_size (AH=3Fh), allocates size/16+1 paragraphs for the output (g_lzw_out_seg/g_lzw_out_base_seg) and 0x40 paragraphs for the input buffer (g_lzw_inbuf_seg), runs lzw_decompress (135a), then frees the input buffer (AH=49h) and closes the handle (AH=3Eh). Returns AX = uncompressed size low word (-1 if zero), BX = output segment. If an allocation failed (g_lzw_out_seg==-1) it jumps to fatal_out_of_memory.

0x53b4.meaning: 4-byte header of an LZW file: uncompressed size

0x53b8.name: g_lzw_handle
0x53b8.meaning: DOS file handle of the file being decompressed (0 = none)

0x53ba.name: g_lzw_out_seg
0x53ba.meaning: current output segment (advances by 1 every 16 bytes); -1 marks out-of-memory

0x53bc.name: g_lzw_out_base_seg
0x53bc.meaning: segment of the allocated output block (returned to caller)

0x53be.name: g_lzw_inbuf_seg
0x53be.meaning: segment of the 1 KB (0x40 paragraph) read buffer

0x53c0.name: g_lzw_dict_seg
0x53c0.meaning: dictionary segment (= g_scratch_seg 0x5354): 3 bytes per code {u16 prefix, u8 char}

0x53c2.name: g_lzw_out_off
0x53c2.meaning: output offset within current output segment (0..15)

0x53c4.name: g_lzw_bitpos
0x53c4.meaning: bit position in the read buffer

0x53ce.name: g_lzw_stack_cnt
0x53ce.meaning: number of chars pushed on the CPU stack for the string being expanded

0x53d0.name: g_lzw_code_limit
0x53d0.meaning: code value at which the code width grows (0x200 initially)

0x53d4.name: g_lzw_first_char
0x53d4.meaning: first char of the previous string

0x53d5.name: g_lzw_last_char
0x53d5.meaning: last decoded char (appended to new dictionary entry)

0x25ea.name: g_raw_file_names
0x25ea.meaning: list of file names stored uncompressed (compared case-insensitively)

notes: INT 21h: 3Dh open, 3Fh read, 3Eh close, 48h/49h alloc/free, 42h seek. Callers: 0bae, 0e94, 0fae, 0ff4.

name: lzw_decompress
purpose: Standard LZW decoder (Ultima V .16/.4/.DAT compression): variable code width 9..12 bits, LSB-first bit packing, code 0x100 = clear/reset, 0x101 = end of data. Reads the file through a 1 KB buffer at g_lzw_inbuf_seg (refilling with INT 21h AH=3Fh when the bit pointer passes 0x3fd bytes, moving the tail to the front), extracts the next code with the mask g_lzw_code_masks[bits-9]. Dictionary at g_lzw_dict_seg:0 with 3 bytes per code (prefix word, char byte), first free code 0x102. Decoded strings are pushed char by char on the CPU stack and written out in order to g_lzw_out_seg:g_lzw_out_off (segment advanced every 16 bytes). Handles the KwKwK case (code >= next_code uses prev string + its first char). After adding an entry, when next_code reaches g_lzw_code_limit the width grows (max 12 bits). On 0x101 the 0x1800-word dictionary area is zeroed and it returns.

0x53b4.meaning: 4-byte header of an LZW file: uncompressed size

0x53b8.name: g_lzw_handle
0x53b8.meaning: DOS file handle of the file being decompressed (0 = none)

0x53ba.name: g_lzw_out_seg
0x53ba.meaning: current output segment (advances by 1 every 16 bytes); -1 marks out-of-memory

0x53bc.name: g_lzw_out_base_seg
0x53bc.meaning: segment of the allocated output block (returned to caller)

0x53be.name: g_lzw_inbuf_seg
0x53be.meaning: segment of the 1 KB (0x40 paragraph) read buffer

0x53c0.name: g_lzw_dict_seg
0x53c0.meaning: dictionary segment (= g_scratch_seg 0x5354): 3 bytes per code {u16 prefix, u8 char}

0x53c2.name: g_lzw_out_off
0x53c2.meaning: output offset within current output segment (0..15)

0x53c4.name: g_lzw_bitpos
0x53c4.meaning: bit position in the read buffer

0x53ce.name: g_lzw_stack_cnt
0x53ce.meaning: number of chars pushed on the CPU stack for the string being expanded

0x53d0.name: g_lzw_code_limit
0x53d0.meaning: code value at which the code width grows (0x200 initially)

0x53d4.name: g_lzw_first_char
0x53d4.meaning: first char of the previous string

0x53d5.name: g_lzw_last_char
0x53d5.meaning: last decoded char (appended to new dictionary entry)

notes: Disassembled from raw bytes 135a-1587 (Ghidra C mangles segment usage). A port needs a bit-exact reimplementation because overlay/data files use it.

name: is_raw_file_name
proto: /* DX=name */ is_raw_file_name() -> CF=1 if name is in g_raw_file_names
purpose: Walks the NUL-pointer-terminated list of string pointers at 0x25ea and compares each case-insensitively (lower-case letters folded to upper) with the name at DS:DX. Returns CF=1 on a full match (name stored uncompressed), CF=0 otherwise. Note Ghidra split this function at 15a5 (artifact); the real body runs 1588-15c4.

0x25ea.name: g_raw_file_names
0x25ea.meaning: names of files that are not LZW-compressed

notes: Ghidra size 29 is wrong (true end 15c4).

name: dos_alloc_top
proto: /* BX=paragraphs */ dos_alloc_top() -> AX=segment, CF=1 on failure
purpose: Allocates BX paragraphs of DOS memory as high as possible. On DOS 3+ (INT 21h AH=30h major==3): sets allocation strategy to best-fit (AH=58h AL=1 BX=2), allocates (AH=48h), restores strategy first-fit (BX=0). On DOS 2: asks for the largest free block (AH=48h BX=-1 fails and returns the max in BX), allocates a filler of (max - request - 1) paragraphs, allocates the request, then frees the filler (AH=49h) - leaving the block at the top of memory. Returns AX=segment with the flags of the real allocation.
notes: Register convention; preserves BX.

name: read_file_into_seg
proto: /* DX=name; stack: seg, size */ read_file_into_seg() -> CF
purpose: Opens the file (AH=3Dh AL=2), reads size bytes into seg:0 (AH=3Fh via 1649) - if size==0 it reads 0xffff bytes, and if the read returned exactly 0xffff bytes it reads one more byte at offset 0xffff - then closes the handle (AH=3Eh). Returns CF=0 on success, CF=1 if the open failed (then the stack args are discarded). Arguments are pushed by the caller as (size, seg) and popped inside.
notes: Unusual stack discipline; only called by 125d and 1d02.

name: dos_read
proto: /* BX=handle, CX=count, DS:DX=buffer */ dos_read() -> AX=bytes read, CF
purpose: Thin wrapper around INT 21h AH=3Fh (read from handle), preserving BX.

name: get_file_size
proto: /* DX=name */ get_file_size() -> DX:AX=size, CF=1 if open failed
purpose: Opens the file (AH=3Dh AL=2), seeks to end (AH=42h AL=2, CX:DX=0) to obtain the size in DX:AX, closes it (AH=3Eh) and returns the size. On open failure returns CF=1 with AX=DOS error.

name: file_exists
purpose: Tries to open the file read/write-shared (AH=3Dh AL=2). If it opens: closes it, clears g_last_dos_error and returns 1. Otherwise stores the DOS error code in g_last_dos_error, calls the far g_error_hook (disk-error UI) and returns 0. Used to check for SAVED.GAM and data files.

0x535c.name: g_last_dos_error
0x535c.meaning: last DOS error code; set to 1 by the INT 24h critical-error handler

0x5394.name: g_error_hook
0x5394.meaning: far pointer to ROOT disk-error handler (1000:2320/2322/25ca)

name: get_current_drive_letter
purpose: INT 21h AH=19h (get default drive, 0=A) and returns 'A'+n.
notes: Called by the disk error handler 2322.

name: put_char
purpose: Writes one character to the current text window (g_cur_window_ptr). Control codes: 0xff clears the window (cursor to 0,0; colour := window bg nibble via driver 15; fill the window's pixel rect (1f77) with driver 21; restore g_cur_color via driver 15), 0xfe toggles underline (g_text_underline, window flag bit0), 0xfd toggles inverse (g_text_inverse, flag bit2), 0xfc sets centred mode (g_text_centred, flag bit1), 0xfb clears it; other values >= 0x80 have bit 7 stripped. 0x0a: cury++ then CR handling; 0x0d: curx=0, and if y0+cury > y1 the window pixel rect is scrolled up 8 pixels with driver 13 (SI=-8) and cury--. Printable chars: glyph offset = ch*8 (ch*24 on Hercules, type 3) in the font segment g_font_seg; the glyph is backed up to g_glyph_backup (17f4) and modified in place for underline/inverse, drawn with driver 31 (AL=x0+curx, BL=y0+cury in cells, DL=fg, DH=bg, ES:DI=glyph), then restored from the backup. If g_cursor_advance (0x538e) is set, curx++ and wraps to a new line when x0+curx > x1.

0x535e.name: g_text_windows
0x535e.meaning: 4 text windows in 8x8 cells: x0,y0,x1,y1 inclusive bounds (default 0,0,39,24), curx/cury cursor relative to x0/y0, attr = bg<<4|fg (default 0x0f), flags bit0 underline, bit1 centred, bit2 inverse

0x539a.name: g_cur_window_ptr
0x539a.meaning: near pointer to current window record in g_text_windows

0x5398.name: g_font_seg
0x5398.meaning: segment of the current font (8 bytes/glyph; 24 on Hercules)

0x538e.name: g_cursor_advance
0x538e.meaning: nonzero = advance cursor after printing (0 while drawing the blinking cursor glyph)

0x52da.name: g_cur_color
0x52da.meaning: current drawing colour restored after clear

0x53ea.name: g_glyph_backup
0x53ea.meaning: copy of the font glyph being drawn (overlaps the 'Out of Memory' string)

notes: Driver 31 reads the glyph from ES:DI (font segment), which is temporarily modified for underline/inverse. Uses FUN_1000_1f77 (window pixel rect) from part2. Callers (115) use it as the basic text primitive.

name: prepare_glyph
proto: void prepare_glyph(/*ES:DI = glyph in font segment*/)
purpose: Copies the glyph (4 words, or 12 on Hercules) from the font segment to g_glyph_backup (0x53ea), then edits the glyph in the font segment in place: if g_text_underline the last row byte (offset 7, or word 0x16 on Hercules) is set to 0xff; if g_text_inverse every word is complemented. put_char restores the original from the backup after drawing.
notes: Register-parameter assembly.

name: print_string
purpose: Prints a NUL-terminated string into the current window with word wrapping. width = x1-x0; for each line: avail = width - curx; copies characters into a 40-byte line buffer until \n, \r, NUL or more than avail chars. If nothing was copied, the control char itself is emitted via put_char (or the loop ends at NUL). If the piece overflows the line it backs up to the last space; if there is none the whole piece is kept and, when curx != 0, a newline is emitted first and leading spaces are skipped; otherwise trailing spaces/CR/LF are trimmed and the separating space is consumed, and a pending newline is remembered if the remaining text was shorter than the line. If the window's centred flag (flags bit1) is set the cursor is moved to column (avail - len)/2 of the current row (set_cursor_pos) before output. Characters are output one by one with put_char. Repeats until the string ends. Used by 250+ callers for all game text.

0x535e.name: g_text_windows
0x535e.meaning: 4 text windows in 8x8 cells: x0,y0,x1,y1 inclusive bounds (default 0,0,39,24), curx/cury cursor relative to x0/y0, attr = bg<<4|fg (default 0x0f), flags bit0 underline, bit1 centred, bit2 inverse

0x539a.name: g_cur_window_ptr

notes: Local 40-byte buffer; line pieces longer than 40 chars are truncated by the avail check (width <= 39). Uses FUN_1000_1f12 (get_cursor_col) from part2.

name: print_number
proto: void print_number(int value, int width, char pad)  /* pascal: [bp+8],[bp+6],[bp+4] */

Digit count = 1 + number of entries in g_pow10[2..5] (10,100,1000,10000) that are <= |value|, plus 1 for a leading '-' when negative. On a file error sets g_last_dos_error, calls g_error_hook and returns 0.

0x535c.meaning: last DOS error code; set to 1 by the INT 24h critical-error handler

0x5394.name: g_error_hook
0x5394.meaning: far pointer to ROOT disk-error handler (1000:2320/2322/25ca)

notes: No callers in the catalog; the RET 2 only pops one word although two are used - likely called with a non-standard sequence or dead code.

name: read_key
purpose: Non-blocking keyboard read. Clears g_key_from_keypad (0x538a). INT 16h AH=1: if no key returns 0. Otherwise reads it with INT 21h AH=6 DL=FF. ASCII key (AL!=0): if it is '1'..'9' and INT 16h AH=2 shows shift/NumLock (flags & 0x23) g_key_from_keypad++; returns the ASCII code. Extended key (AL==0): reads the scan code; scan codes 0x3b..0x44 (F1-F10) return scan+0x8e (0xc9..0xd2); scan codes in g_scan_table (0x540e: K M H P G O I Q = left,right,up,down,home,end,pgup,pgdn) are translated via g_scan_xlat (0x5416: 1,2,3,4,0xd3..0xd6) with g_key_from_keypad++; anything else returns 0. Finally, if g_flush_after_key (0x538c) is set the keyboard buffer is flushed.

0x538a.name: g_key_from_keypad
0x538a.meaning: nonzero if the key came from the numeric keypad / arrow keys

0x538c.name: g_flush_after_key
0x538c.meaning: nonzero = flush type-ahead after each key (toggled in COMBAT)

0x5416.name: g_scan_xlat
0x5416.meaning: internal codes 1,2,3,4,d3,d4,d5,d6 for the scan codes

notes: INT 16h AH=1/2, INT 21h AH=6.

name: wait_key
purpose: mode 0: blocks until poll_key_with_cursor returns a key (animated cursor while waiting). mode 1: a single poll. mode N>1: up to N polls (returns 0 if none), temporarily setting g_cpu_speed to 500 so the per-poll delay (20fa) is longer. Returns the key code.

name: read_line
purpose: Line editor: loops on wait_key(0); Backspace (8) or key code 1 (left arrow) with n>0 erases one char (FUN_1000_1fa0(1)) and n--; ESC (0x1b) erases all n chars; printable 0x20..0x7f with n<maxlen is stored and echoed with put_char. Ends on Enter (0x0d); buf[n]=0.
notes: Ghidra call site FONT: FUN_1e38(8,buf) = read_line(buf,8).

name: set_default_drive
proto: int set_default_drive(char letter)  /* pascal; 1 ok, 0 fail */
purpose: Clears g_last_dos_error; validates/uppercases the letter (1ef7: must be A..Z, DL=index); INT 21h AH=0Eh selects the drive; if no critical error occurred and INT 21h AH=19h reports the same drive (stored in g_cur_drive 0x541e) returns 1. Otherwise sets g_last_dos_error=1, calls g_error_hook and returns 0.
